title: Contact
metaTitle: Contact Us | Sell North Dakota Mineral Rights
metaDescription: Reach a fourth-generation North Dakota ranch family directly to talk through your mineral interest, no obligation and no pressure to decide today.
heroLead: Whether you have a question about a division order or you're ready to talk numbers, reaching us is a phone call or a short form away, not a maze of departments.
intro: We answer our own calls. When you reach out about your North Dakota mineral interest, you're talking to someone from our family, not a call center reading from a script, and not a rotating cast of representatives who've never seen your county before. That's on purpose. It's the same way we'd want to be treated if the situation were reversed.

sections.heading: What to have ready
paragraphs: A conversation goes faster if you have a rough idea of which county your minerals are in and roughly how many net mineral acres you own, though it's completely fine to reach out without that information and figure it out together. If you have a recent royalty statement, division order, or deed handy, that helps too, but none of it is required for a first conversation.

If you're not sure what you own, or you inherited an interest and are still sorting out the paperwork, that's a common starting point and exactly the kind of situation we're used to walking through with people.

sections.heading: What happens after you reach out
paragraphs: We'll ask a few questions about your acreage, the county, and whether it's leased or producing, then look at county records and any documentation you're able to share. From there we'll give you a straightforward sense of where things stand, whether that's a preliminary number, a request for a few more documents, or an honest answer that we need more information before we can say anything useful.
There's no obligation attached to a first conversation, and we're not going to push you toward a decision on a timeline that doesn't work for you or your family.

sections.heading: For families with shared ownership
paragraphs: If your mineral interest is split among siblings, cousins, or other heirs, feel free to reach out even if you're just one of several owners trying to get a sense of value for the family. We're used to coordinating with multiple owners and can walk through how that process typically works when more than one person needs to sign off.
We're also happy to answer general questions even if you're not ready to sell anything right now. Understanding what you own is a reasonable first step on its own.

sections.heading: If you're reaching out from out of state
paragraphs: A good share of the North Dakota mineral owners we hear from live in another state entirely, sometimes having never set foot on the land their family owns minerals under. That's completely normal for interests that passed down through inheritance, and we handle the entire process, from the first conversation through closing, without requiring you to travel to North Dakota.

Documents can be reviewed, signed, and returned by mail, and we're glad to talk through the process by phone at whatever pace makes sense for you, whether that's one call or several over a few weeks while you gather what you need.

sections.heading: No pressure, just information
paragraphs: We know mineral rights can feel confusing, especially if you inherited an interest without much explanation of what it actually involves. Our goal in a first conversation is simply to help you understand what you have, not to rush you toward a decision. If it takes several conversations over a few months before you're ready to move forward, or if you decide not to sell at all, that's a fine outcome too.

Some of the most useful calls we have are with people who just want to understand their own paperwork, a division order that doesn't make sense or a royalty statement that dropped without explanation, with no plan to sell at all. We're glad to have that conversation too, and we'll never turn it into a sales pitch you didn't ask for, even if it means the call ends with nothing more than a clearer picture of what you own.

faqs.question: Is there any cost or obligation to contact you?
faqs.answer: No, reaching out for a conversation or a preliminary look at your minerals costs nothing and doesn't obligate you to sell.

faqs.question: What's the best way to reach you?
faqs.answer: Use the contact form on this site or call the number listed, and someone from our team will follow up directly rather than routing you through an automated system.

faqs.question: Do you respond quickly?
faqs.answer: We typically respond within a business day or two. If your situation is time-sensitive, mention that when you reach out.

faqs.question: Can I reach out even if I'm not sure what I own?
faqs.answer: Yes, plenty of people who contact us are still sorting out what they inherited. We can help figure out the county and rough acreage from what documentation you do have.

faqs.question: Can multiple family members join the same conversation?
faqs.answer: Yes, we're happy to get on a call with more than one owner at a time, or to follow up separately with each family member as they have questions, whichever works better for your family.
